title: Check yourself: Rolling out: plugins, servers, spend and adoption

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Scenario: Yusuf's organisation limit is 20000 a month and covers three groups. Yusuf proposes limits of 7000, 8000 and 6000 for them. What does the page say about that proposal?

options.text: It is sound, because the organisation limit stops any overspend by the groups
options.says: Ruled out because "so the organisation limit would decide before the group limits did and nobody would know which one they were under".

options.text: It breaks the arithmetic, since the parts could together exceed the whole
options.says: Seven thousand, eight thousand and six thousand add up to 21000, which is more than 20000.

options.text: It is sound, because unused budget of one group is lent to the others
options.says: Ruled out because the page requires that "The group limits add up to the organisation limit and no more", and says nothing about lending.

options.text: It is inconsistent, since each group must have the same limit as the others
options.says: Ruled out because the page's own example has "three groups with 6000, 8000 and 6000 against an organisation limit of 20000", so equal limits are not required.

questions.stem: Scenario: A platform team wants to show leadership that Claude Code is working. It sets a target of more accepted lines per developer each month and starts the rollout on Monday. What is the main weakness of the plan?

options.text: Accepted lines are not shown on the dashboard and cannot be tracked
options.says: Ruled out because "The dashboard counts lines accepted as a usage metric".

options.text: Developers accept fewer lines as they learn, so the figure falls over time
options.says: Ruled out because the page gives no such trend and rests on the point that "lines accepted can be raised by accepting more lines".

options.text: A monthly target is too coarse to reflect how developers actually work
options.says: Ruled out because the page's objection is "A target on an activity invites the activity", not the length of the period.

options.text: Activity rises without any gain, so the figure proves nothing
